facts.text: Mogadore’s name comes from Mogador, Morocco, inspired by the book Sufferings in Africa, a memoir of a captured ship captain.
The village’s first settler, Ariel Bradley, was only nine when he served as a spy for George Washington during the Revolution.
Before the Civil War, Mogadore served as a station on the Underground Railroad, helping enslaved people seek freedom.
Between 1820 and 1850, Mogadore hosted two flour mills, a carding mill, saw mills, barrel factories, distilleries, a wheelwright, blacksmith, and tannery.
Mogadore maintains a public library branch of the Akron‑Summit County Public Library, serving the local community.
